title: Shared KAN parents with sparse private edge residuals
hypothesis: A shared KAN parent plus small private rational residuals only on exceptional edges preserves all heldout functions with lower complete bytes than independent edge functions and beats ordinary GS-KAN plus KAN residual controls.

world.private_residual: one Gaussian rational bump per exceptional edge

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after native residual alias or complete-byte gate failure.

controls: Mirror edge codes plus sparse private bump residuals
native GS-KAN parent plus standard rational residuals
success_gate: heldout nRMSE <=0.02, >=25% fewer complete bytes than independent edges, and strict quality/byte/compute advantage over native GS-KAN + rational residual.
failure_gate: FAIL if native residual parameterization matches Mirror or full-byte gate misses.
boundaries: Synthetic analytic scalar functions only; no trained KAN claim.
Exceptional edge IDs are known and charged; no anomaly selection claim.
No fresh samples after native residual alias or gate failure.
